 2 weather alerts in effect DOH warns of recalled ashwagandha capsules sold in Hawaii over salmonella risk 
 DOH said the recalled product was available at Hawaii Whole Foods stores and online through Amazon from Nov. 24, 2025, through Oct. 20, 2026. (Hawaii Department of Health) By HNN Staff Published : Nov. 4, 2026 at 9:10 PM HST | Updated : 21 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - The state Department of Health (DOH) Food and Drug Branch (FDB) is warning consumers about an herbal supplement sold at Whole Foods Market stores in Hawaii.
 Vitality Works Inc. issued a recall of its 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha Capsules, 120-count, due to potential salmonella contamination.
 DOH said the recalled product was available at Hawaii Whole Foods stores and online through Amazon from Nov. 24, 2025, through Oct. 20, 2026.
 The product was sold in white plastic bottles labeled as 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha 120 count, with UPC 9948252099. Consumers can identify the product by lot number 2025-26227 and expiration date “10/13/2028,” both printed on the bottom of the bottle.
 Consumers can identify the product by lot number 2025-26227 and expiration date “10/13/2028,” both printed on the bottom of the bottle, along with the UPC 9948252099. (Hawaii Department of Health) FDB said it is working with local stores to ensure the recalled product is no longer available for sale.
 Health officials said those infected with Salmonella may experience symptoms including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea or bloody diarrhea, abdominal cramping and fever. In some cases, Salmonella infection can lead to more serious but rare conditions, such as arterial infections, endocarditis, arthritis, muscle pain, eye irritation and urinary tract symptoms. Children, older adults and individuals with compromised immune systems are at greater risk of severe illness.
 Anyone experiencing symptoms after consuming the recalled product should contact their healthcare provider immediately.
 FDB advises anyone who purchased the product to check the UPC on the label, along with the lot number and expiration date printed on the bottom of the bottle. Recalled products should not be consumed and should be discarded.
 Officials said refunds are available at any Whole Foods Market store. Consumers with questions can contact Vitality Works Inc. at 505-268-9950 Monday through Friday from 5 a.m. to 2 p.m. Hawaii time.
